blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In complex transactions — multi-jurisdiction deals, long delivery windows, specialist commodities, or trust arrangements with multiple buyers and sellers — letters of credit are rarely used in their textbook form. They are stacked, amended, transferred and layered with further instruments, each chosen for a specific risk.

A transferable LC allows the original beneficiary to pass part of the credit to a second-tier supplier. A back-to-back LC issues a new credit against the security of an existing one. A standby LC functions more like a guarantee than a payment instrument. In large commodity trades, all three may appear in the same structure, each serving a narrow purpose.

The discipline at this level is conceptual rather than clerical. Every instrument should answer one simple question: which risk does it cover, and for whom? When that question cannot be answered cleanly, the structure should be redesigned, not patched. The most expensive LC disputes one ever sees began with a structure that grew by accident, one amendment at a time, until no one could still describe what it was for.

items.q: According to the text, why are letters of credit rarely used in their textbook form in complex transactions?
options: Because they are stacked, amended and layered with other instruments for specific risks
Because standby LCs have replaced all other forms
Because banks refuse to issue them across jurisdictions
Because commodity trades do not require documentary credit
items.why: "They are stacked, amended, transferred and layered with further instruments, each chosen for a specific risk."

items.q: What does a back-to-back LC do?
options: It converts a transferable LC into a standby LC
It issues a new credit against the security of an existing one
It passes part of the credit to a second-tier supplier
It functions as a guarantee rather than a payment instrument
items.why: "A back-to-back LC issues a new credit against the security of an existing one."

items.q: The text says a standby LC functions more like a guarantee. This suggests that…
options: it replaces the need for a transferable LC
it is expected to be called only if something goes wrong
it is normally drawn on for routine payment
it cannot appear alongside other instruments
items.why: Inferência: uma garantia é acionada em caso de falha — não no fluxo normal de pagamento, ao contrário de um instrumento de pagamento.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Each instrument in a structure should cover a clearly named risk
A structure that cannot be described cleanly is best fixed with one more amendment
Expensive disputes often start with structures that grew by accident
The discipline of structuring LCs is conceptual, not clerical
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente "redesigned, not patched" — remendar com mais uma alteração é justamente o que o autor condena.

items.q: What does the final sentence about disputes imply about complexity?
options: Unmanaged, accidental complexity is a source of costly risk
Complexity is always the sign of a sophisticated deal
Amendments are illegal in commodity trades
Only standby LCs cause disputes
items.why: Inferência: estruturas que crescem "by accident, one amendment at a time" geram as disputas mais caras — a complexidade sem propósito é o perigo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie revisando a estrutura de LCs de um negócio de açúcar. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me talk you through what I'm seeing on this sugar deal, because I'm not comfortable signing it off yet. We have a transferable LC from the end buyer, and against that we've opened a back-to-back to the mill. On paper it holds together.

My problem is the amendments. There have been four since we opened, and each one solved a small local issue, but nobody stepped back to check the whole thing still made sense. Two of the amendments actually shifted risk back onto us without anyone flagging it.

Honestly, we should have redesigned this a month ago instead of patching it. If the shipment had been delayed by even a week, the back-to-back might have expired before the transferable was drawn, and we'd have been exposed on both sides.

So here's what I want. Before another amendment goes out, I need one page that says, for each instrument, which risk it covers and for whom. If we can't write that page cleanly, we don't amend — we rebuild the structure from scratch.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Sophie not comfortable signing off on the deal yet?
options: The amendments were made without checking the whole structure still made sense
There is no transferable LC in place
The end buyer has not confirmed the price
The mill refused the back-to-back LC
items.why: "each one solved a small local issue, but nobody stepped back to check the whole thing still made sense."

items.q: What does Sophie say two of the amendments did?
options: They cancelled the back-to-back LC
They reduced the value of the credit
They shifted risk back onto her side without anyone flagging it
They extended the delivery window safely
items.why: "Two of the amendments actually shifted risk back onto us without anyone flagging it."

items.q: When Sophie says "we should have redesigned this a month ago instead of patching it," she is…
options: expressing regret about a past decision
describing what the buyer demanded
explaining a bank regulation
praising the team's careful work
items.why: Inferência: "should have redesigned" é passado hipotético — ela lamenta que a estrutura não tenha sido refeita a tempo.

items.q: What was the risk if the shipment had been delayed by a week?
options: The back-to-back might have expired before the transferable was drawn, leaving them exposed
The mill would have raised its price
The standby LC would have been triggered automatically
The end buyer would have cancelled the order
items.why: "the back-to-back might have expired before the transferable was drawn, and we'd have been exposed on both sides."

items.q: What is Sophie's rule before any further amendment goes out?
options: All amendments must be translated into two languages
The end buyer must approve every change
The mill must issue a fresh standby LC
One page must state, for each instrument, which risk it covers and for whom
items.why: "I need one page that says, for each instrument, which risk it covers and for whom." É a mesma pergunta central da lição.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The mill was named as a second-tier supplier under a transferable LC." A transferable LC lets the original beneficiary…
options: issue a guarantee against default
convert the credit into cash immediately
cancel the credit at any time
pass part of the credit to another supplier
items.why: LC transferível permite que o beneficiário original repasse parte do crédito a um fornecedor de segundo nível.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "They opened a ___ against the security of the buyer's original credit, so the mill could be paid."
options: standby LC
spot contract
back-to-back LC
bill of lading
items.why: LC back-to-back = novo crédito emitido com base na garantia de um crédito já existente.

items.q: "This was a multi-jurisdiction deal." This means the transaction…
options: had only one counterparty
was priced above market
involved several legal jurisdictions
used a single currency
items.why: Multi-jurisdiction = multijurisdicional: envolve mais de um ordenamento jurídico.

items.q: "We kept adding fixes, but you can only patch a structure so many times before it fails." To patch here means to…
options: translate the documents
make small local fixes instead of a proper redesign
formally approve the credit
cancel the transaction
items.why: To patch = remendar: resolver pontualmente sem repensar a estrutura como um todo.

items.q: "Each amendment looked harmless on its own." An amendment is…
options: the maturity date
a formal change to the terms of the credit
a shipping document
a new counterparty
items.why: Amendment = alteração formal nos termos do LC.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre estruturas de crédito documentário. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The treasurer still has to sign off on the structure before we open the credits." To sign off on means to…
options: postpone indefinitely
publish externally
formally approve
quietly criticise
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's not just patch over the problem with another amendment." To patch over something means to…
options: explain it in detail to the board
escalate it to the regulator
cancel the whole transaction
cover it superficially without fixing the cause
items.why: Patch over = tapar o problema de forma superficial, sem tratar a causa.

items.q: "Two of the amendments shifted risk onto us." This means the changes…
options: moved the exposure onto our side
had no effect on risk
reduced our exposure
clarified who was liable
items.why: Shift risk onto someone = transferir a exposição para o lado daquela parte.

items.q: "Before we go further, let's step back and look at the whole structure." To step back means to…
options: withdraw from the deal
pause to see the bigger picture
reverse the last amendment
delegate the work
items.why: Step back = afastar-se do detalhe para enxergar o conjunto.

items.q: "If we can't describe it cleanly, we start from scratch." To start from scratch means to…
options: make one final amendment
ask the buyer to decide
keep the current structure
begin again from the beginning
items.why: Start from scratch = recomeçar do zero, redesenhar em vez de remendar.
